claims.text: ChainPoll achieves an aggregate AUROC of 0.781 on the RealHall benchmark suite.
ChainPoll outperforms the next best theoretical algorithm by 11% in aggregate AUROC on RealHall.
ChainPoll exceeds industry standards for LLMs by over 23% in aggregate AUROC on RealHall.
ChainPoll-Correctness achieves an average AUROC of 0.772 for open-domain hallucination detection on RealHall Open.
ChainPoll-Adherence achieves an average AUROC of 0.789 for closed-domain hallucination detection on RealHall Closed.
GPT-4 disagreement rate with human annotators on hallucination detection is equal to or lower than the inter-human annotator disagreement rate.
ChainPoll computes a metric score by prompting an LLM multiple times with detailed chain-of-thought and taking the fraction of positive boolean judgments.
Pseudo-entropy retains unnormalized probability mass in the log-probability term to estimate entropy when only top-M token probabilities are available.

evidence.description: Table 1 shows ChainPoll achieved an aggregate AUROC of 0.781 on RealHall across benchmarks.
ChainPoll's aggregate AUROC of 0.781 beats the next best method SelfCheck-Bertscore (0.673) by 0.108 AUROC (11%).
Section 1.1 states ChainPoll beats industry standards for LLMs by over 23%.
Table 3 reports ChainPoll-Correctness achieving an average AUROC of 0.772 on RealHall Open.
Table 4 reports ChainPoll-Adherence achieving an average AUROC of 0.789 on RealHall Closed.
Appendix A.3 notes that GPT-4 disagreed with human annotators no more often than the human annotators disagreed with one another.
Section 4.2 defines ChainPoll as running gpt-3.5-turbo with a detailed CoT prompt multiple times and dividing the 'yes' answers by the total runs.
Appendix A.4 defines pseudo-entropy as -sum(\tilde{p} * log(p)), preserving probability mass information lost by normalizing probabilities beforehand.

methodologies.name: ChainPoll
methodologies.description: A hallucination detection metric that uses detailed chain-of-thought sampling over multiple completions from gpt-3.5-turbo to compute a boolean agreement ratio.

methodologies.name: RealHall Benchmark Suite
methodologies.description: A hallucination detection benchmark suite consisting of four datasets curated for challenge, realism, and task diversity across open-domain and closed-domain settings.

limitations.text: Prior academic benchmarks for hallucination detection rely on summaries and completions generated by older, weaker models that produce obvious hallucinations unlike modern SOTA LLMs.
Academic hallucination metrics predominantly focus on closed-domain tasks, neglecting open-domain hallucination detection.
ChainPoll is constrained to black-box settings and cannot utilize model-internal information such as weights, activations, or embeddings.
Probability-based metrics like pseudo-entropy are restricted by commercial API limitations that only return probabilities for a top subset of tokens.
